Read the passages very carefully and then choose the best alternative based on the explicit and implicit messages they convey and blacken the letter of your choice in the space provided in the answer sheet Reading Passage Haddis Alemayehu: A Pioneer of Ethiopian Literature Haddis Alemayehu is one of Ethiopia’s most respected writers, widely known for his contribution to modern Ethiopian literature. Born in 1909, he was not only a novelist but also a diplomat and public servant. His life experiences in politics, education, and international relations greatly influenced his writing. Through his literary works, Haddis Alemayehu explored Ethiopian society with depth and realism. His most famous novel, Fikir Eske Mekabir (Love unto Grave), is considered a masterpiece of Amharic literature. The novel presents a tragic love story while also addressing social class differences, tradition, and injustice. The author skillfully portrays human emotions and moral conflicts, making the story both touching and thought- provoking. The novel remains widely read and studied in Ethiopian schools and universities. One of the strengths of Haddis Alemayehu’s writing is his profound understanding of Ethiopian culture and values. He used literature as a tool to criticize harmful traditions and to promote social awareness. His works reflect the struggles of ordinary people and challenge readers to think critically about society. This enduring relevance is one reason his writing continues to influence new generations. Beyond literature, Haddis Alemayehu served his country in various leadership roles, including as Ethiopia’s ambassador to the United States and the United Nations. His ability to combine artistic talent with public service made him a unique figure in Ethiopian history. Today, he is remembered not only as a great writer but also as a national intellectual whose ideas still inspire discussion and reflection. Source: Alemayehu, Haddis. Fikir Eske Mekabir (Love unto Grave). 1968
